macroNarrative: The macro backdrop has deteriorated measurably since our last edition: Brent crude has surged past $107 on Iran-shock oil fears, the rupee has hit a fresh record low of nearly 96/USD, and both Nifty and Sensex are under pressure. The dual shock of elevated crude and a weak rupee squeezes OMCs, aviation, and import-heavy manufacturers while providing a tailwind to upstream energy, pharma exporters, and IT. The family corpus must hold its nerve — the domestic earnings cycle remains healthy, the rate-cut cycle has done its work, and selectivity between crude-winners and crude-losers is now the most important portfolio decision.

conviction.name: HDFC Bank
conviction.thesis: India's largest private-sector bank, finally past its post-merger digestion. Asset quality is at a multi-year best, the governance review is clearing, and the franchise's deposit-gathering machine is unmatched. The valuation has stopped being demanding.
catalysts: Governance review clearing path for CEO reappointment
NIM stabilisation post HDFC Ltd merger absorption
Branch-led deposit growth re-accelerating
Retail credit cycle turning supportive in FY27
risks: Net interest margin pressure if RBI eases further
Credit costs in unsecured retail
Heavy index weight invites foreign-flow volatility

conviction.name: ICICI Bank
conviction.thesis: The best-run large bank in India by almost any operating metric — consistent ROA above 2%, conservative provisioning, a digital stack peers are still trying to replicate. Weekly stock performance remains relatively resilient. We pay a premium happily.
catalysts: Industry-leading return on assets >2%
Cleaner book than every private peer
Fee income compounding at double digits
FII return to India likely to favour ICICI first among large banks
risks: Valuation premium leaves less room for error
Slowing retail unsecured credit growth
Macroprudential tightening overhang

conviction.name: State Bank of India
conviction.thesis: The flagship PSU has seen a 10% weekly return setback per live feeds — likely macro-driven, not fundamental. Asset quality is at its cleanest in a decade, ROE has migrated above 16%, and it trades at roughly 1.5× book. We use this weakness to hold steady, not panic.
catalysts: Cleanest GNPA/NNPA ratios in 10+ years
Subsidiary value (SBI Cards, SBI Life, AMC) under-counted in price
Beneficiary of credit growth in a high-crude environment
Valuation gap vs private peers remains wide
risks: Government cross-currents (PSL targets, minority stake sales)
Treasury volatility in rate cycle turns
Slower fee-income growth than private peers

conviction.name: ITC
conviction.thesis: A cash-printing cigarette monopoly funding a steadily compounding FMCG business, plus hotels, paperboards, and agri. Near-zero debt, a 3.5%+ dividend yield, and a hotels demerger that should unlock value the consolidated structure has long obscured.
catalysts: Hotels demerger value unlock crystallising
FMCG margins continuing to expand toward HUL's
Cigarette taxation cycle relatively benign
Rupee weakness irrelevant — domestic revenue base is the hedge
risks: Cigarette regulation / taxation surprises
FMCG rural demand recovery has been uneven
Tobacco-related ESG screens limit some institutional buying

conviction.name: Bharat Electronics
conviction.thesis: The crown jewel of Indian defence indigenisation. Order book over ₹75,000 Cr giving multi-year revenue visibility, ROCE above 25%, debt-free balance sheet. India-Pakistan border tensions and elevated geopolitical risk globally only reinforce the structural demand case for domestic defence spending.
catalysts: Defence capex growing at low-double digits in FY27 budget
Export orders compounding from a small base
Order book : revenue ratio above 3×
Geopolitical tension elevating indigenous defence procurement urgency
risks: Valuation multiple is the highest in its history
Order timing inherently lumpy
Margin pressure from competitive bidding

conviction.name: Power Finance Corp
conviction.thesis: Government-backed NBFC at the centre of India's power and renewables financing build-out. Trades at a single-digit P/E with a ~4% dividend yield, ROE in the high teens, and a loan book with vastly improved asset quality after the Discom clean-up.
catalysts: Renewable energy financing the dominant growth driver
Asset quality at cyclical best
Re-rating potential as discom risk is repriced
Elevated crude accelerates India's push to renewables — more financing demand
risks: Concentration in power sector / discom credit risk
Tariff / regulatory interventions
Bond market volatility on long-dated lending book

conviction.name: Oil & Natural Gas Corp
conviction.thesis: Brent at $107+ is the most direct upgrade to ONGC's earnings picture. Weekly return of ~6% confirms the market is repricing this. At P/E ~7.5× and P/B ~1×, with crude elevated and the windfall-tax regime now better-understood, ONGC is the cleanest crude-hedge in the portfolio.
catalysts: Brent persistently above $100 lifts realisations materially
Windfall tax regime more stable than feared
Gas price reform supporting earnings floor
Iran oil shock sustaining crude at elevated levels
risks: Sharp crude correction if geopolitical risk eases suddenly
Government windfall taxes can re-emerge at $100+
Capex cycle pressure on free cash flow

conviction.name: Coforge
conviction.thesis: The bright spot in a battered IT sector. Deal wins are accelerating and the AI/cloud positioning is pulling clients from the giants. Rupee weakness at 96/USD provides a meaningful tailwind to reported rupee earnings — one of the few IT names where the macro shift now works in our favour.
catalysts: Deal wins outpacing Tier-1 IT
AI services book gaining real revenue traction
Cigniti acquisition synergies still ahead
INR at 96/USD adds ~200bps to rupee revenue growth
risks: IT sector sentiment remains poor — multiple compression risk
Concentration in BFSI vertical
Higher beta than large-cap IT in any global slowdown

conviction.name: Bajaj Auto
conviction.thesis: Export-led two-wheeler franchise with strong April sales momentum. Importantly, petrol price hikes now underway post fuel-price rise will provide some near-term headwind to two-wheeler volume sentiment, but Bajaj's export diversification and CNG/EV mix reduce the sensitivity versus domestic-only peers.
catalysts: Export tailwind back after a multi-year drought — 83% YoY in April
EV (Chetak) reaching meaningful volumes
CNG + 3W commercial cycle underway
Less domestic fuel-price sensitivity than Hero/TVS peers
risks: Petrol price hike dampens domestic two-wheeler demand near-term
EV margin profile still being established
Africa/LatAm currency exposure on exports

conviction.name: Reliance Industries
conviction.thesis: The default India mega-cap, with three engines now visible: Jio (telecom + monetisation), Reliance Retail (largest retailer in the country), and a maturing oil-to-chemicals business. Crude at $107 is a mixed signal — supportive for O2C margins, but watch for retail energy cost pass-through.
catalysts: Jio tariff hike cycle still has runway
Reliance Retail IPO talk persists as latent catalyst
New energy capex starting to produce revenue
O2C margin uplift as GRM widens with crude spike
risks: Capital intensity remains very high
Quick-commerce competition pressuring retail margins
Conglomerate discount may persist longer than expected

longBets.name: Syrma SGS Technology
longBets.thesis: Top brokerage pick in Indian Electronics Manufacturing Services. The sector grew 24% CAGR FY19-24 and is forecast at 27% to FY29 on PLI schemes and China+1 supply-chain shifts. Margin expansion is structural as backward integration deepens. India's EMS market share is under 5% globally — it is heading higher.
catalysts: FY26-28E revenue CAGR estimated at 29%, profit CAGR 44% by HDFC Sec
PLI scheme extension expected; budget tailwinds
Aerospace/defence/healthcare mix shift improving margins by 130bps
OSAT (semiconductor packaging) optionality being scoped
risks: Dependence on imported components; rupee at 96 raises input costs
Cost competitiveness vs. China & Vietnam
Single-quarter margin volatility on input costs
Sector valuations have run hard

longBets.name: Praj Industries
longBets.thesis: India's largest biofuel technology company. Crude at $107 is an unambiguous positive for biofuel economics — the E20 ethanol blending mandate becomes even more strategically imperative at high oil prices. The temporary order pause that caused the 30% drawdown looks increasingly like a 'Mr. Market' moment.
catalysts: E20 ethanol blending program scaling — crude above $100 accelerates urgency
SAF commercialisation underway globally
Order book recovering after temporary pause
High crude environment improves biofuel project economics
risks: Lumpy project order cycle
Recent quarterly loss reflects execution slippage
Sharp crude correction would dampen biofuel economics

longBets.name: Data Patterns (India)
longBets.thesis: Q4 revenue declined 13% YoY to ₹345 Cr — a significant miss, and the stock is down 11% today. This is precisely the lumpy quarterly revenue risk we flagged. However, the thesis has NOT broken: the franchise quality, the order pipeline, the margin structure, and the policy tailwind are all intact. This is an entry window for those who don't own it, not an exit.
catalysts: FY27 budget targeting 'Force Multipliers' (electronic warfare, drone swarms)
Order pipeline remains substantial despite quarterly lumpiness
Margin guidance 35-40% structurally unchanged
Tejas Mk1A and indigenous platform build-out multi-year
risks: Q4 revenue miss confirms lumpy quarterly execution — patience required
Valuation at 60×+ requires consistent delivery
Higher beta — 40%+ annualised volatility; today's 11% drop is characteristic

longBets.name: MTAR Technologies
longBets.thesis: High-precision component supplier to defence, aerospace, civilian nuclear, and clean energy (fuel cells, electrolysers). Niche, hard-to-replicate manufacturing capabilities. Recently won a $3.78m order in data-centre infrastructure, opening a new vertical.
catalysts: Defence indigenisation orders compounding
Clean energy fuel-cell components scaling globally
Order book healthy across multiple verticals
Data-centre vertical opens new TAM
risks: Valuation at 165× P/E is the most stretched among peers
Margin profile choppy (10% ROE)
Single new-vertical bets carry execution risk

longBets.name: Astra Microwave Products
longBets.thesis: RF and microwave subsystems for radars, electronic warfare, and satellite payloads. Q3 FY26 profit jumped 96% QoQ; operating margins expanded to 31.7%. Trades cheaper than peers. Geopolitical escalation globally and India's own border situation are structural tailwinds for indigenous radar and EW procurement.
catalysts: 12.4% rise in DRDO R&D funding for indigenous AESA radars
Q3 margins jumped to 31.7% on better mix
Geopolitical tensions structurally accelerating indigenous defence spending
Relatively cheaper vs Data Patterns on P/E basis
risks: Stock recently in technical downtrend
ROE at 10.5% lags Garden Reach (20%) and Data Patterns (13%)
Beta of 1.35 means sharper drawdowns in selloffs

longBets.name: KNR Constructions
longBets.thesis: Roads and highways EPC contractor with one of the cleanest balance sheets in the construction space. Government's NHAI awards remain a reliable pipeline, and KNR has consistently delivered above-industry execution. At 13.5× earnings, the valuation is genuinely undemanding.
catalysts: NHAI award pipeline remains strong
Debt-free working capital management
Margin profile better than larger peers
Government infrastructure push unchanged despite crude headwinds
risks: Asset monetisation pace slower than hoped
Order inflows concentrated in NHAI
Construction cycle exposure to monsoon delays

longBets.name: Maharashtra Seamless
longBets.thesis: India's largest seamless pipe manufacturer for oil & gas, power, and infrastructure. Crude at $107+ directly accelerates domestic upstream capex — ONGC, Oil India, and private E&P companies will step up drilling and pipeline activity, which is the primary demand driver for Maharashtra Seamless.
catalysts: Domestic oil & gas capex ramping — Brent at $107 is a direct demand driver
Export market widening
Debt-free balance sheet allows organic capex
14× P/E remains very undemanding for the earnings profile
risks: Steel price volatility
Cyclical demand patterns
Concentration in oil & gas customer base

longBets.name: Ion Exchange (India)
longBets.thesis: Pioneer in water and wastewater treatment in India. ROCE of 27.5%, debt-equity 0.2, operating across municipal, industrial, and household water. Direct beneficiary of Jal Jeevan Mission and increasingly stringent industrial effluent norms.
catalysts: Jal Jeevan Mission and similar government water programs
Industrial effluent compliance becoming mandatory
Premium consumer water purifier brand (Zero B)
Domestic revenue base — fully insulated from rupee weakness
risks: Project execution timing
Working capital intensity in EPC contracts
Smaller order sizes vs MNC competitors

highPromise.name: Computer Age Management Services
highPromise.thesis: A duopoly providing the picks-and-shovels for India's mutual fund industry. Q4 EBITDA margin expanded to 46.3%, profit grew 11%. As MF AUM compounds at 15%+ annually, CAMS rides that wave with operating leverage. NSE EGR trading commencing May 18 is an incremental product catalyst.
catalysts: MF industry AUM growth structural at 15%+
New product wins (alt fund servicing, AIFs, EGRs)
Best-in-class operating margins
NSE Electronic Gold Receipts platform launch a new fee pool
risks: Pricing pressure from large MFs
Regulatory caps on RTA fees
Concentration in top-5 AMC clients

highPromise.name: Wockhardt
highPromise.thesis: Posted a turnaround Q4 — ₹164 Cr profit versus a ₹45 Cr loss a year ago. The novel antibiotic pipeline (Zaynich, others) is reaching commercial inflection. Speculative but asymmetric.
catalysts: Zaynich US launch progress
Specialty antibiotic pipeline maturing
Operating leverage as losses recede
Rupee weakness incrementally favourable for US export revenues
risks: History of inconsistent execution
Balance sheet still recovering
Regulatory / FDA process risk

highPromise.name: Himachal Futuristic
highPromise.thesis: Optical fibre cable, 5G transmission gear, and a small but growing defence electronics order book. India's 5G + BharatNet + defence comms theme captured in one mid-cap name.
catalysts: BharatNet phase 3 ramp
5G private network orders
Defence segment scaling from a small base
risks: Working-capital intensive
Order timing volatile
Margin pressure from raw material moves and rupee weakness on imports

highPromise.name: Suzlon Energy
highPromise.thesis: A fully restructured balance sheet, the largest order book in its history, and a wind capacity addition cycle just starting after years of dormancy. Brent at $107+ is the most powerful political tailwind for accelerating India's domestic renewable energy push — Suzlon is a direct beneficiary.
catalysts: Order book at multi-year highs
Net-debt-free for the first time in a decade
Wind add-back cycle in FY27–28
High crude prices accelerate government push to domestic wind and solar
risks: Single-product, single-geography concentration
Execution risk on large orders
Investor base still partly speculative

highPromise.name: IdeaForge Technology
highPromise.thesis: Pure-play on Indian military and homeland-security drone procurement, an area where indigenisation policy is accelerating. Revenue inflection confirmed with a 7× YoY surge and return to profit. Geopolitical tension elevating near-term procurement urgency is an incremental positive.
catalysts: Defence drone orders multi-year visible
Revenue inflection just confirmed
Limited domestic competition
Border tensions elevating drone procurement urgency
risks: Lumpy order cycle
Tiny float, very volatile
Margin sustainability unproven at scale

watchClose.name: Tata Consultancy Services
watchClose.thesis: The bluest of blue chips, but caught in a sector-wide air pocket. Rupee at 96/USD is a tailwind to reported INR revenues. Quality of business is unchanged; what has changed is the cyclical demand picture from US BFSI clients. We hold; we do not chase.
catalysts: Buyback / dividend yield supports floor
AI services adoption with marquee clients
INR at 96/USD meaningfully aids reported rupee earnings
risks: US client spending caution lingers
Wage inflation if attrition climbs again
Premium multiple vs. growth trajectory

watchClose.name: Infosys
watchClose.thesis: Same story as TCS, slightly cheaper. Operating margins are pinched, but the franchise, balance sheet and capital return habit are intact. Rupee tailwind at 96/USD is supportive. Not a sell, just not yet a buy.
catalysts: AI / cloud deal momentum
Margin recovery as discretionary spend returns
Steady buyback cadence
risks: Global IT budget compression continues
Onsite cost pressure
Sector de-rating not yet over

watchClose.name: Hindustan Unilever
watchClose.thesis: Volume growth has returned and the FY27 outlook is brighter — but at ~55× earnings, you are paying for a perfect recovery. The gold import duty tightening has a minor read-through for premium categories. Trim, don't add.
catalysts: Rural demand recovery gathering pace
Premiumisation across categories
Margin recovery once palm oil cools
risks: Valuation leaves no room for misses
Quick-commerce reshaping distribution economics
Private label encroachment

watchClose.name: Asian Paints
watchClose.thesis: The franchise is real, the brand is real — but Birla Opus remains the most credible threat to the moat in twenty years. Until we see how share-loss settles, holding is the right answer; adding is not.
catalysts: Decorative volume growth recovery
Industrial paints scaling
Margin defence playbook intact
risks: Birla Opus competitive intensity
Multi-quarter market share concession likely
Multiple still rich for the new growth profile

watchClose.name: Larsen & Toubro
watchClose.thesis: Guided FY27 revenue growth lower on Middle East disruptions — and Brent at $107 means West Asia tensions are not dissipating soon. The long-cycle infra story is unchanged; the near-term margin and order-timing headwinds are real. Hold; let the dust settle.
catalysts: Domestic infra & defence order pipeline intact
Hyderabad campus / IT services value
Middle East order book recovery once tensions ease
risks: West Asia exposure to conflict risk — worsened by Iran oil shock
Margin guidance has been reset down
Capex slowdown if elections shift policy

watchClose.name: Bharti Airtel
watchClose.thesis: Best-positioned in a duopoly, with strong ARPU momentum and Africa optionality. But the stock has already priced much of the next two years of tariff hikes. We hold what we have; we don't add aggressively here.
catalysts: ARPU compounding into ₹240+
5G monetisation begins
Africa cash flow turning material
risks: Capex demands remain heavy
Regulatory / spectrum costs
Premium valuation vs. global telecom peers

trimAvoid.name: Trent
trimAvoid.thesis: Zudio is a brilliant business; Trent at this price is a brilliant business priced as if it cannot stumble. Single-month drawdowns of 22% in such names are reminders that valuation matters. Trim into strength.
catalysts: Store rollout still aggressive
Brand strength in value fashion
risks: P/E above 100× is structurally hard to defend
Saturation in Tier-1 cities arriving
Any same-store-sales miss is asymmetrically punished

trimAvoid.name: Avenue Supermarts
trimAvoid.thesis: A great business with a slowing growth equation. Quick-commerce is reshaping the urban grocery basket faster than DMart's store-led model can respond. The valuation still assumes the old growth trajectory; the new one is materially lower.
catalysts: Steady store additions
Best-in-class working capital
risks: Quick-commerce eating high-frequency baskets
Same-store-sales-growth slowing
Multiple still 80–90× earnings

trimAvoid.name: Nestle India
trimAvoid.thesis: An exceptional brand portfolio at a price that demands exceptional growth — which has not been delivered. Volume growth has been mid-single-digit; the multiple is double that of global staples. Hold a small position at most.
catalysts: Pricing power intact
Distribution expansion in smaller towns
risks: Valuation vs. growth gap is the largest in years
Royalty hike overhang reappears periodically
Premium FMCG demand softening

trimAvoid.name: Eternal (Zomato)
trimAvoid.thesis: Blinkit is genuinely interesting; the valuation prices in it being interesting forever. With Swiggy and Reliance escalating quick-commerce capex, the path to durable profitability is narrower than the share price suggests. Elevated crude raises delivery economics pressure.
catalysts: Blinkit GMV scaling rapidly
Going-out / events business optionality
risks: Quick-commerce profitability still unproven at scale
Capex war intensifying; crude at $107 raises delivery cost
Loss-making segments still subsidised

trimAvoid.name: Titan Company
trimAvoid.thesis: Titan's near-term outlook has darkened on two simultaneous hits: gold at ~$4,572/oz (even after today's 3% fall, gold remains elevated in rupee terms at a record-weak INR) and the Centre tightening duty-free gold import norms. The 2013 playbook shows jewellery volumes can contract sharply when gold prices surge and import duties tighten. At current valuations, the risk-reward has deteriorated.
catalysts: Brand strength and store rollout intact long-term
Non-jewellery categories (watches, eyewear) provide some offset
risks: Gold import duty tightening squeezes jewellery margins and volumes
Gold price in INR near all-time highs — demand elasticity negative
Valuation premium under threat if earnings estimates cut

trimAvoid.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corp
trimAvoid.thesis: Brent at $107+ with a petrol and diesel price hike already announced puts HPCL in a painful position — marketing margins are structurally compressed at high crude, and any further hike will face political resistance. The recent stock decline of 3%+ on fuel price hike news reflects markets pricing in margin erosion. Avoid while crude stays elevated.
catalysts: Refining margins could widen if product cracks hold
Government subsidy backstop in extremis
risks: Marketing margin squeeze as Brent stays above $100
Government resistance to full retail price pass-through
Rupee weakness at 96/USD amplifies crude import cost

sectors.name: Private Banking
sectors.note: Asset quality at a decadal best; rate-cut cycle essentially done. Reasonable valuations on the leaders; FII return likely to favour this sector.

sectors.name: PSU Banking
sectors.note: Cleanest books in years, single-digit P/Es on the largest names. SBI's 10% weekly setback looks macro-driven, not fundamental.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.note: INR at 96/USD is a meaningful earnings tailwind for exporters; partially offsets demand caution from US clients.

sectors.name: FMCG
sectors.note: Recovery underway but priced into most names. Gold duty tightening a mild headwind for premium consumer spend.

sectors.name: Auto
sectors.note: Petrol/diesel price hikes a near-term headwind to domestic two-wheeler demand; export-heavy players (Bajaj) more insulated.

sectors.name: Pharma
sectors.note: US generics cycle stable, domestic chronic therapy compounding. Rupee at 96/USD is a structural export earnings booster.

sectors.name: Real Estate
sectors.note: Rate cuts flowing through; inventory cycle remains supportive in top-7 cities. Crude has limited direct impact here.

sectors.name: Capital Goods / Infra
sectors.note: Domestic order books healthy; Middle East execution risk elevated with Iran oil shock. L&T guidance reset is a caution flag.

sectors.name: Energy / Oil & Gas
sectors.note: Brent at $107 is a strong earnings upgrade for upstream (ONGC, Oil India). OMCs facing margin squeeze — bifurcate clearly.

sectors.name: Defence
sectors.note: Geopolitical tension globally and domestically accelerates indigenous procurement. Data Patterns Q4 miss is lumpy execution, not thesis.

sectors.name: Renewables
sectors.note: Crude at $107 is the strongest political argument for accelerating domestic renewables — wind and solar capacity addition urgency rises.

sectors.name: Quick-Commerce / Internet
sectors.note: Capex war intensifying; elevated crude raises last-mile delivery costs. Path to profit is narrowing, not widening.

earnings.watch: Q4 results out; Goldman Sachs and Nomura commentary — read for defence order cadence

earnings.name: Tata Motors PV
earnings.watch: Q4 net profit -32% YoY; JLR margins and India PV outlook key — brokerages split

earnings.name: Kaynes Technology
earnings.watch: Down 25% in two sessions; watch for brokerage target cuts and EMS sector read-through

earnings.name: Data Patterns
earnings.watch: Q4 revenue -13% YoY to ₹345 Cr — lumpy execution; monitor order pipeline commentary

earnings.name: Cipla
earnings.watch: US Lanreotide ramp, India branded generics growth, margin guidance

earnings.name: ONGC
earnings.watch: FY26 exit realisations and FY27 capex guidance with Brent at $107

earnings.name: Adani Enterprises
earnings.watch: New energy capex progress, airport revenue ramp, green hydrogen timeline

earnings.name: UltraTech Cement
earnings.watch: Volume growth, realisation per tonne, capacity utilisation commentary

earnings.watch: Jewellery volume guidance post gold duty tightening; management commentary on demand

whispers.text: Brent at $107 on Iran oil shock is the dominant macro variable this week — bifurcating winners (upstream, biofuels, renewables) from losers (OMCs, aviation, two-wheeler domestic demand, quick-commerce delivery costs).
INR hit a record low of 95.94/USD today — a double-edged sword: tailwind for IT, pharma, and upstream exporters; headwind for import-heavy sectors and the macro current account.
Petrol and diesel prices hiked; analysts warning further rises likely. Near-term headwind to two-wheeler volumes, transportation costs, and rural discretionary spend.
HAL Q4 results and Data Patterns revenue miss are quarterly noise; the multi-year indigenisation order pipeline is structurally intact and geopolitical tension only deepens the mandate.

Centre tightening duty-free gold imports is a near-term headwind for Titan, Kalyan, Senco — watch jewellery volume guidance carefully. Gold in INR terms near all-time highs amplifies demand elasticity pressure.
Kaynes Technology down 25% in two sessions; China chip rally sparking valuation bubble fears globally. Indian EMS valuations may face compression even as the long-term structural story holds.

Electronic Gold Receipts commence trading May 18 — a new financial product that could channel gold investment through exchange platforms. Monitor for impact on physical jewellery demand and CAMS fee pool.
